mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.00% in a given month coincides with a near-term decline in S&P 500 20-day forward returns due to higher discount rates eroding expected future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.00% in the current month
regime_hint: Rising Fed Funds rate surprises in late-cycle expansion
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, 20-day forward returns remain statistically indistinguishable from pre-shock levels (p > 0.10), or the FEDFUNDS spike is not confirmed by a contemporaneous S&P 500 decline.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE by more than 0.10 percentage points while employment momentum (PAYEMS) remains stable is associated with a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as lower labor market tightness reduces growth risk.
regime_hint: Early-stage labor market moderation after a strong cycle
failure_condition: In 60-day windows where UNRATE rises >0.10 but PAYEMS shows accelerating growth, forward returns are negative or no better than random chance (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) growth exceeding +2.0% over three months predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as it signals robust economic momentum and reduced recession risk.
failure_condition: Three-month INDPRO acceleration never materializes, or 60-day forward returns remain flat or negative despite other positive signals.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly falls by more than 0.5% month-over-month, S&P 500 20-day forward returns turn negative due to market anticipation of rate cuts and weaker wage growth pressures.
regime_hint: Unexpected disinflation during a tightening cycle
failure_condition: Over 20 consecutive months of CPIAUCSL declines > -0.5%, forward returns never turn positive or show no statistically significant deviation from baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in reserve balances (RSAFS) of more than 1,000 million dollars over two consecutive months coincides with a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as markets anticipate future policy easing.
regime_hint: Declining reserve liquidity in a steady-rate environment
failure_condition: RSAFS declines persist but forward returns remain flat or negative, or the S&P 500 shows no mean reversion over the 60-day window.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) exceeding 200,000 while UNRATE remains below 4.0% predicts a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return as weak labor demand increases recession risk.
regime_hint: Labor market cooling in a low-rate environment
failure_condition: In 20-day windows where unemployment claims rise >200k but UNRATE stays below 4%, forward returns are not statistically worse than baseline (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month surge in housing starts (not directly observable in the provided proxies, but as a domain signal, a decline in HOUST by >10% coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return via risk-off sentiment about economic activity.
regime_hint: Sharp contraction in building activity as a leading indicator
failure_condition: HOUST declines >10% are not followed by statistically significant negative 20-day forward returns (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls by more than 3.0% in a month while the S&P 500 60-day forward return is negative, this reflects a supply-side shock that precedes and amplifies market pessimism, supporting a regime-conditional negative return signal.
regime_hint: Structural supply disruption during a growth slowdown
failure_condition: Over 30 such INDPRO declines, the 60-day forward return never turns positive or shows mean reversion (p > 0.05).
